# Hytale RPG Master Implementation Specification

Version 1.1 • Codex execution authority • Source freeze: S1 v1.3 / S2 v0.5 • UI/HUD contract update

## Execution map

**Scope:** 87 active skills • 66 passives • 14 gated phases • 95 documented particle candidates.

**Primary instruction:** Phase 00 first. Pin the repository/build, prove the required UI and runtime capabilities, then stop for approval.

**Art policy:** Every skill and passive uses a shipped icon template. Every effect has a functional visual fallback. Artist-created replacements are independent of mechanics readiness.

**Authority:** Explicit master decisions resolve inherited conflicts. Source excerpts and candidate assets are not treated as proof of implemented gameplay.

| Read location | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- |
| Sections 00-02 | Authority, schema and runtime boundaries |
| Sections 03-05 | Stats, resources, combat, XP and acquisition formulas |
| Sections 06-08 | Passive compiler, Link Tree/Character/HUD UI contracts and no-bottleneck art system |
| Section 09 | All 87 active execution and visual records |
| Section 10 | All 66 passive effects, gates and fixtures |
| Sections 11-14 | Phases, tests, rollout, worked examples and evidence limits |
| Appendices A-D | Numeric tables, coverage, supplied images and sources |

# 00\. Authority, provenance and execution boundary

This is the consolidated implementation contract for the classless Hytale RPG and its Link Tree. It replaces the two frozen source snapshots as the execution reference for this implementation program, without deleting or silently modifying either living source file. A future source edit is not automatically a runtime change: produce a versioned reconciliation before adopting it. S1 owns gameplay intent; S2 supplies existing skill/passive behaviour. Explicit Master Decisions (MD) below resolve conflicts and fill missing rules at the user's request. All new numeric rules are initial balance values, not measured gameplay results.

All 87 active skill records and 66 passive records are included. Thirteen retired monster-anatomy concepts remain excluded. Phantasm is a naming reservation, not a defined active skill. Arc remains an illustrative compatibility example, not a 67th passive. There are no permanent player classes, class gates, class-owned trees or class-specific base attributes. Four logical equipped skills, six total passive nodes and two routing joints define the build surface. Every skill can exist without any links. All six passives may strengthen one skill.

Terms MUST, MUST NOT and REQUIRED are normative. NEW BASELINE identifies a master-authored decision. DOCUMENTED CANDIDATE is an external asset name that has not been tested in the installed build. VERIFIED\_ASSET requires a local catalog/hash check; VERIFIED\_CONNECTED additionally requires a recorded in-game test. PLANNED is never synonymous with implemented. ART\_TEMPLATE is not an error or a mechanics blocker.

This document does not certify that the repository compiles, that Hytale exposes every requested UI primitive, or that any listed particle looks appropriate without inspection. Phase 00 obtains that evidence. Work proceeds one authorised phase or cohort at a time. Do not automatically progress from one completed stage to the next, rewrite unrelated mods, reset saves, push main, or deploy merely because a local test passes. Preserve existing Tavern/Orbis systems behind narrow adapters; the LLM is not involved in combat authority.

## 00.1 Source freeze and retention

The input files were fetched from their original Drive IDs, not inferred from earlier chat copies. Their hashes, revisions, source URLs and a source-to-master map are included at the end. Ordered paragraph/table extracts are shipped in references so inherited text remains inspectable. Existing source formulas and descriptions are retained except for explicitly listed corrections and per-skill closures. Source notes such as “exact formula undefined” are not execution instructions when this master supplies that formula.

## 00.2 Master Decision register

| ID | Source gap or conflict | Canonical master decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| MD-01 | 10 starting attribute points plus source pool formulas produce more than the stated 100-point level-1 pools. | Pool scaling uses E(raw)-E(10). Damage/healing scaling retains 1+0.003 E. No automatic per-level pool increment is introduced. |
| MD-02 | Rewarding enemies from the complete XP-to-next formula cancels its late-game grind multiplier. | Enemy rewards use the unpressured 100 L^1.6 base; the cubic endgame term applies only to level requirements. Rank multipliers are retained. Kill-count targets are interpolated between band endpoints to avoid lower XP rewards immediately across a biome boundary. |
| MD-03 | Earlier documents asserted Ability 4 was available in a particular prerelease. | The fetched public enums did not independently confirm that claim. Bind only capabilities proven in the pinned server/client build. Preserve logical slot 4 even when disabled; no control hijacking. |
| MD-04 | Art “content-blocking TODO” contradicts the user's requirement not to wait for bespoke art. | Missing candidate art resolves to shipped project templates. Mechanics/telegraph readability must work; final illustrations and signature art are a separate backlog. Missing all valid fallback presentation is still a content-preflight failure. |
| MD-05 | Weapon-dependent skills sometimes hardcode Light or Heavy despite accepting both. | Weapon skills resolve the audited held/offhand item class; no-weapon skills use an explicit fixed scaling attribute. Healing/absorb skills use WIS as specified. |

# 01\. Build audit, modules and schemas

## 01.1 Phase 00 evidence manifest

Record repository origin/branch/HEAD, working-tree status, server version, client version, SDK JAR hash, Java toolchain, asset archive hash, world/save schema, dependency versions and operating system. Use the current clean repository; never reset to an old reference revision from a source document. A pre-release experiment lives in a separate adapter/profile and does not modify production saves. W13/W14 list public interaction enums; their names alone do not prove a client binding or event path.

Create build-capabilities.json with booleans and evidence paths for: authoritative entity stats; damage phases; custom damage causes; hit outcome observation; per-item native attack classification; projectile collision/steering; selective collision boundaries; NPC ownership/allegiance restoration; corpse/death records; CustomUIHud creation/update/removal; native HudComponent Health/Mana/Stamina visibility control; custom page open/close/event flow; native Inventory-page augmentation; pointer-drag coordinates; pointer capture; clipped pannable panel; spline or segmented-line rendering; hovered-entry keyboard events; arbitrary/global keyboard bindings; C reverse-camera/machinima binding removal or remap; C Character binding; K Link Tree binding; Ability 1..4; native ability-slot backend. Public Page.Inventory and Page.Custom are distinct \[W24\]; therefore native Inventory augmentation remains UNPROVEN until a concrete supported extension path is demonstrated. Unsupported capabilities disable only their adapter/family, with a named blocker. Do not fabricate a Java method, enum constant, client keybinding facility or particle ID to satisfy this document.

## 01.2 Proposed module boundaries

| Module | Owns | Does not own |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| rpg.domain | IDs, immutable definitions, stat math, graph types, pure compatibility rules | Hytale ECS mutation, UI rendering |
| rpg.content | Versioned catalogs, normalization, preflight, signatures and migrations | Invented asset names or runtime guesses |
| rpg.progress | XP, allocation, mastery, learned skills, passive ownership, reward ledger | Native current Mana/Stamina/Health duplication |
| rpg.links | Graph validation, effect-plan compilation, modifier ordering | Player permissions, raw pointer positions as mechanics |
| rpg.combat | Cast lifecycle, hit queries, outcomes, status and trigger budgets | Client particle collision as damage |
| rpg.hytale | Narrow SDK-specific adapter implementations and capability probes | Independent alternate armor/HP engine |
| rpg.presentation | HUD/canvas, icon resolver, VFX/audio ownership | Acquiring skills or applying damage |
| rpg.integration | Optional Kingdoms rest provider and external party/protection providers | Hard dependency on future Kingdoms or HTDevLib |

Proposed names are project namespaces, not assertions about existing repository classes. Reuse equivalent existing services where ownership matches; record the mapping before adding duplicates. No database or asset download runs synchronous ly in the world tick. Content compilation is pure and cacheable by definitions hash \+ graph revision \+ relevant equipment profile revision.

All requests are intentions: equip known SkillId, allocate delta, connect NodeIds, submit graph revision. Server verifies ownership, points, slot counts, target validity and version. A client-supplied absolute level/stat/damage/cooldown is never accepted. Allocation conservation: sum(allocated)+unspent \=5\*(level-1)+explicit Quest Point Awards. pendingLevelUpPoints is a nonnegative subset of unspentAttributePoints: each newly earned character level adds 5 to both counters; attribute allocation consumes pendingLevelUpPoints first. The Level Up HUD notice remains until pendingLevelUpPoints reaches 0\. Existing-save migration initializes pendingLevelUpPoints to 0 unless a trustworthy level-up ledger exists; do not fabricate historical pending points. Level is derived from total XP thresholds and must agree with its stored cache.

Hytale EntityStatMap remains the authority for live Health/Mana/Stamina. Save only the necessary native persistence references and RPG modifiers/ledgers, not a competing current-resource object. The default progression scope is the persistent server/save UUID plus authenticated player UUID; worlds within that server share progress unless an explicit per-world profile is selected. A single writer owns each player revision, with compare-and-swap updates and stale-client rejection. Durable writes are atomic with monotonic revisions and checksums; migration writes a backup and a new file before replacement. On failure, refuse progression changes rather than resetting to level 1\. A bounded journal gives exactly-once rewards after restart. Database-backed storage is an optional adapter, not a Firebase requirement. The threat model is an untrusted remote player against a trusted server; singleplayer machine owners are not tamper-proof.

# 02\. Effect taxonomy and shared runtime

S1 distinguishes delivery/space, behaviour, payload, element/status and timing. Preserve that layering. Primary executors are Strike, Projectile, DirectTarget, Burst, Cone, Line, Beam, GroundZone, Wall, Trap, Movement, Aura, Barrier, Summon, Corpse Operation, Stance and Reaction. Orb/Orbit and Bombardment/Overhead reuse spatial/timing primitives. Mark, Curse, Buff, Vortex and Imbue are parameterized payload/state combinations, not mandatory new engines for each name. Transformation remains reserved because its only active source skill was retired.

Projectile is a travelling collision carrier. Line is a ray/front/sweep, even when visually streaked. Burst is one radial resolve. GroundZone is terrain-anchored and finite. Aura is caster-attached and sustained by Mana drain or reservation. A finite MobileZone does not become an Aura. A self-only Aura may lack HasRadius. Collision Radius and EffectRadius are distinct typed fields. SpellCast is an authored execution capability, not inferred merely from Mana cost or Magic damage.

## 02.1 Units, geometry and targeting

World distance is expressed in metres in content; Phase 00 calibrates its Hytale-world-unit mapping and records it. Angles in content are degrees; adapters use radians only at explicit conversion. Simulation time is seconds, independent of render frame rate. Core gameplay ticks use delta-time accounting; active effects receive one scheduler owner. No per-frame unbounded timers, no sleep calls on world threads.

NEW BASELINE geometry defaults: ground area height 3 m; humanoid strike/line/cone height 2.5 m; ground anchor follows one legal surface, not every floor of a building. Circular footprints use cylinders, not hidden spheres. Full width is never interpreted as radius. Cone membership uses horizontal distance, vertical bounds and the dot-product half-angle test. Radial falloff is absent unless declared. Target shape uses collision bounds, not a guessed model centre. Swept queries prevent tunnelling for dash/projectile motion.

All hostile effects require loaded, permitted, alive non-friendly targets and LOS from the effect's permitted origin. Friendly effects include caster unless declared otherwise and only currently allied recipients. Party/faction/protection adapters are authoritative; absence defaults to no player-vs-player damage. Ground target validation rejects unreachable surfaces behind walls or ceilings. No skill destroys/builds terrain by default. Displacement stops before obstacles, respects nav/height limits and never moves protected NPCs or across world boundaries.

Projectile outgoing lifetime defaults to maxDistance/speed; an explicit independent time cap wins if shorter. Travel distance is total traversed path, not displacement from spawn, so Chain/Homing cannot make an immortal shot. Outbound and Return have separate bounded legs and ledgers. No-weapon physical/magic skills use authored INNATE power; they do not read a random held weapon.

## 02.2 Cast state machine

IDLE \-\> VALIDATING \-\> WINDUP \-\> COMMIT \-\> \[DELAYED\] \-\> RELEASE  
     \-\> ACTIVE / DERIVED\_EXECUTIONS \-\> TERMINATING \-\> TERMINATED

Before commit: resolve equipment/ownership/gates, validate current target and reserved object claims, predict complete plan cost and root budget. Failure consumes nothing. Wind-up can be interrupted without a charge. At COMMIT revalidate and atomically charge the single resource plus any ammunition/item token; start cooldown, capture offensive stats/equipment/plan and a valid target solution. One pending primary release per slot. Skill Delay waits 2 s after COMMIT, not before affordability checking. Post-commit death/logout/unload/equipment incompatibility cancels owned work without refund. Rejected derived work does not refund the paid root.

At RELEASE: target-point casts use the committed world point; origin-based actions use current actor position but revalidate the point is still within allowed reach/LOS. Aim direction is snapshotted. Melee and movement revalidate live geometry. Echo repeats use the committed solution, not a newly improved target silently chosen later. Kill Trigger is the explicit retargeting exception. If an original target dies, invalid direct-target repeats disappear; ground repeats can still resolve at their valid world point. Switching worlds always cancels.

Damage/healing/CC resolution, particle spawning and sound are separate callbacks under the same owner. Animation is feedback, not a second damage source. Native attack interactions must be suppressed or instrumented so an RPG hit never lands twice. Every accepted cancel and completion is idempotent. Projectile miss expiration, normal effect expiry, budget truncation and forced cancellation have different terminal reasons; explosion-on-expiry passives cannot treat all four as “OnKill.”

# 03\. Attribute, resource, reservation and recovery math

All coefficients are balance-profile data. Inputs must be finite; raw attributes are nonnegative. Equipment and temporary attribute bonuses enter the same curve, without bypassing diminishing returns. Preserve fractional effective stats and resource values internally; round only at explicit integer-cost/XP boundaries. The HUD shows one decimal where a new point would otherwise look ineffective.

E(A) \= min(max(A,0),150)  
     \+ .75\*clamp(A-150,0,100) \+ .50\*clamp(A-250,0,100)  
     \+ .35\*clamp(A-350,0,100) \+ .20\*max(A-450,0)  
MaxHealth  \= max(1, 100 \+ 2.00\*(E(STR)-E(10)) \+ FlatHealth)  
MaxStamina \= max(1, 100 \+ 0.50\*(E(DEX)-E(10)) \+ FlatStamina)  
TotalMaxMana \= max(1, 100 \+ 0.75\*(E(INT)-E(10)) \+ FlatMana)  
AttributeDamageMultiplier \= 1 \+ .003\*E(resolvedDamageAttribute)  
HealingMultiplier \= 1 \+ .003\*E(WIS)

MD-01 yields level 1 exactly 100 Health/100 Stamina/100 Mana before gear, and all-in raw 500 gives 720 Health, 255 Stamina or 332.5 Mana respectively. Those are independent specializations, not one character receiving all three simultaneously. At raw 150/250/350/450, marginal attribute efficiency changes from 1 to.75/.50/.35/.20. With base 10 and 5 points/level, all-in arrival levels are 29/49/69/89. Point 451 is diminished; point 450 still contributes. Basic pool growth has no hidden class coefficient.

Weapon class resolution: Light=Swords/Daggers/Bows/Crossbows/Guns/Bombs \-\>DEX; Heavy=Longswords/Maces/Battleaxes/Spears/Shields \-\>STR; Magic=Staffs/Wands/Spellbooks \-\>INT. Names are user-facing categories, not authoritative ItemIds. Resolve explicit mod tags or a pinned registry; the SDK's DamageClass.Light/Charged/Signature is a separate attack-mode axis. For mixed allowed weapon types, choose the actually equipped item's class. Healing and absorb calculations use WIS independently of the weapon's damage attribute.

## 03.1 Secondary stats and complete percentage semantics

WisdomHaste \= .30\*E(WIS)/(E(WIS)+160)  
FinalCooldown \= max(.25, BaseCooldown\*DurationFactors /  
                    (1+clamp(WisdomHaste+RecoveryBonuses,0,.75)))  
LearnBonus \= min(.40, .0015\*E(WIS))  
CritChance \= clamp(.05 \+ .25\*E(LUCK)/(E(LUCK)+250)+FlatCrit, 0, .75)  
CritMultiplier \= max(1, 1.50 \+ FlatCriticalMultiplierBonus)  
UpgradeBonus \= .10\*E(LUCK)/(E(LUCK)+300)  
UpgradeChance \= clamp(BaseUpgradeChance+UpgradeBonus, .01, .95)  
MagicFind \= max(0, .005\*E(LUCK)+GearMagicFind)

Recovery rate is not cooldown reduction. A 15% recovery bonus divides a cooldown by 1.15; a 15% longer enemy cooldown multiplies duration by 1.15. Keep elapsed cooldown work when recovery rates change; do not restart it. NEW BASELINE total haste cap 75%, total crit cap 75%; source attribute components keep their original saturation. Accuracy: first implementation is deterministic geometric collision, with no random miss roll after a confirmed contact. Dexterity grants no hidden accuracy bonus. Debuff resistance comes from explicit status/encounter profiles, not an undocumented Intelligence effect.

Magic Find affects optional quality weights only: Normal weight remains unchanged; Uncommon weight\*(1+min(MF, 1.0)); Rare\*(1+min(MF,.75)); Unique\*(1+min(MF,.50)); renormalize the existing quality distribution. It does not increase item count, Signature Learn Chance, unique-source availability or deterministic quest rewards. Until an upgrade/quality adapter exists, show those stats as inactive rather than modifying vanilla loot blindly. Initial upgrade base chances for ranks 1..10 are max(.20,.95-.075\*(rank-1)); unsuccessful upgrades consume the authored materials but do not destroy/downgrade the item. No upgrade feature ships without a versioned material recipe and explicit item opt-in.

## 03.2 Single authoritative resource loop

Passive regeneration is 1.5% of the current total maximum per second for Mana and Stamina. A valid root normal weapon hit returns 4% of each; a valid root fully charged basic weapon hit returns 12% of each. The weapon's Light/Heavy/Magic scaling class does not restrict which pool returns. One attack hitting eight targets returns once. A skill such as Snipe counts as fully charged for allowed skill interactions but is not a free basic-attack refund event. Reflections, summons, DoTs, friendly damage, invulnerable targets, self-costs and repeat children never earn this basic refund.

Native sprint/block actions and native regeneration must be audited after Stamina is raised to 100\. The adapter records their actual units and suppresses only duplicate regen sources, not unrelated mechanics. Preserve native traversal/block behaviour through a scale-normalization profile where necessary, then test exhaustion. For fixed-unit native Stamina costs, the initial normalization factor is 100 divided by the audited original maximum; percentage-based native costs are not multiplied again. No silent 10x increase in sprint/block endurance is assumed merely because the pool baseline changes. Health has no new passive regeneration in this mod by default; native food/rest rules remain separately accounted for.

## 03.3 Mana reservation and Managuard

For each active reservation Aura i: Reserved\_i=TotalMaxMana\*compiled Fraction\_i; sum them using total pre-reservation Mana, not successively shrinking percentages. Spendable Max Mana=TotalMaxMana-sum(Reserved). Reject totals above 100%, and require current spendable Mana sufficient to establish new reservation. Activation moves capacity into reserved state and removes that amount from current spendable Mana. Releasing a reservation reopens capacity but does not generate current Mana. Regeneration and safe rest stop at Spendable Max Mana. No negative reservation, recursion from Mana-maximum Auras or capacity feedback loop is permitted.

Conservation and Resonance modify fractions before fit validation. A reduced Mana maximum can invalidate reservations: disable the most recently activated reservation first until feasible; notify the user, never silently exceed max. Fractional reservation precision is retained. Cosmetic meter segments never become authoritative resource values. Save allocation revisions and activation ordering; do not automatically resume damaging Auras on login before validation.

Managuard reserves 1..50% selected in 1% steps, default 50%; initial base shield equals actual reserved Mana. Damage depletes shield, not reservation. NEW BASELINE: after 6 s without hostile damage, recharge at 10% of current shield capacity per second. A saved deficit ledger survives toggle, loadout change and reconnect; toggling cannot restore the shield. New capacity \= current reserved amount times eligible barrier modifiers; current shield=max(0, newCapacity-deficit), capped to newCapacity. Lowering/re-raising capacity never erases deficit. Recharge reduces deficit, including while not equipped at the last validated rate only in eligible out-of-combat time; if time evidence is unavailable, no offline recharge is credited. Existing shield-capacity modifiers may increase capacity above raw reserved amount; the unmodified base remains 1:1.

Emanatism modifies passive Mana regeneration rate by 25% Increased; it does not amplify on-hit returns, leech or Stamina. Identical named Auras use the strongest valid effect per recipient. Different permitted recovery effects add in the stated Increased bucket. Reservation does not grant the shield or Aura to all allies unless its family/target contract says so.

## 03.4 Rest and Kingdoms compatibility

Successful rest in the player's verified own bed immediately restores spendable Mana and Stamina. Home-region restoration requires 2 s continuous presence and no hostile damage dealt/received for 3 s, plus no active hostile target/encounter lock. W11's home signal is not proof of personal house ownership: verify the saved bed owner/location. Do not infer “home” from arbitrary blocks or a nearby stranger's bed. Future Kingdoms providers may authorize owned/shared-home or kingdom rest volumes; providers return actor, volume, permission, expiry and safety evidence. No hard dependency, no entire-kingdom combat refill by default. A revoked provider immediately loses authority.

# 04\. Combat resolution, statuses and protection

## 04.1 Base power and complete hit equation

Weapon Base Power comes from a versioned audited per-item RPG power registry BEFORE RPG attributes, mastery, crit, attack charge or native bonus damage. A development test weapon has 20 base power. Magic weapon authored MagicPower defaults to 20 in development; pure HealingPower defaults 20\. Innate damaging skills default 20 unless their own closure defines another number. Production item records explicitly select the base number; unknown production weapons are unsupported, not auto-guessed by name or copied from post-mitigation hits.

PreMitigation \= BasePower \* AttributeMultiplier \* MasteryMultiplier  
              \* SkillCoefficient \* max(0,1+sum(Increased)-sum(Reduced))  
              \* product(MoreFactors) \* product(1-LessFractions)  
              \* (critical ? CriticalMultiplier : 1\)

MoreFactors are direct multipliers, e.g.1.35, whereas Less Fractions are fractions, e.g..10. Raw fields must encode their operator, never an ambiguous “+effect.” Native cause/armor/resistance filtering occurs once after offensive calculation. Submit damage via the pinned Hytale damage lifecycle and consume actual results after application \[W07\]. Do not subtract target armor twice, reapply weapon charge, or let a native attack emit an untracked parallel hit. Where the SDK itself scales damage, the adapter must prove an idempotent path or disable the family.

Mastery Multiplier=1+.02\*(skillLevel-1), skillLevel 1..20. Only damage/healing/barrier magnitude uses this multiplier initially; no hidden range, proc chance, reservation efficiency, ally haste or CC scaling. Conditional victim-health/CC modifiers are checked when that target's damage is gathered, not on cast snapshot. Elemental split fractions sum to 1; compute one offensive total, split by channel, then apply channel-specific mitigation. Critical roll is server-owned and keyed by root/execution/contact. Periodic damage and reflection do not crit by default. Multi-projectile/multi-hit proc Coefficient=1/authored simultaneous count unless explicitly set; this changes proc chances, not hit damage.

Damage types are project-owned semantic IDs. Frost maps to COLD; Arcane to MAGIC; Shadow to VOID; NECROTIC and NATURE remain distinct authored channels. Each maps to a locally verified native/custom DamageCause asset. Missing mapping blocks that content profile, not silently converts everything into Physical. Protection, team and story/quest immunity is checked before outgoing effects and again at damage application.

Healing=min(final Requested Healing, missingHP); overheal is separately available only to Overflow. Absorb capacity has owner/expiry and cannot stack copies of the same caster+skill unboundedly. Default replacement keeps the greater current shield, capped to current created capacity, rather than adding. Spirit Shield redirect splits already mitigated damage exactly once; transferred damage cannot recursively redirect or be mitigated a second time. Reflected packets carry Reflect/NoProc/NoLeech/NoCredit tags. Resource costs are not damage events.

## 04.2 Status math and stack ownership

| Status | Initial magnitude / lifetime | Ownership and application |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Chill | 5% movement slow per stack; maximum 5; shared 6 s expiry refreshed by legal application | At 5 consume all and apply Frozen. Multiple source stacks share the victim threshold; record contribution provenance. |
| Frozen | Movement disabled 2 s; attacks/casts interrupted and disabled during freeze | After thaw, Frozen immunity 3 s; Chill may build to 4 during immunity but cannot freeze until a later legal application. Boss substitute is Slow, never Frozen. |
| Burn | .10\*resolved offensive base power per second; source-specific duration (default 4 s) | One per caster+skill+victim; stronger snapshot refreshes, weaker refresh does not reduce DPS. Tick 1 s, proportional final remainder. |
| Poison | .06\*resolved offensive base power per stack per second; default 6 s | Basecap 3 per caster+skill+victim; applications addone and refresh that source package; max 12 total victim stacks with strongest-package replacement deterministic. Virulence addsone/application; Concentrated Venom modifies only that sourcecap. |
| Bleed | From Hemorrhage:12% triggering pre-mitigation Physical hit per second for 4 s | One strongest per caster+skill+victim; no crit, movement multiplier or recursive proc. |
| Root | No voluntary translation; turning/attacking allowed; duration from skill | Direct block/terrain collision still authoritative; protected entities reject. |
| Fear | Retreat under navigable AI request, no teleport; initial skill duration | Direct damage after 0.25 s grace breaks it. DoT does not. No hard Fear on boss/player/protected actor. |
| Stagger/Stun | Interrupt action and prevent restart for allowed duration | Repeated-control scaling below; do not mutate animation playback to simulate cooldown. |
| Taunt | Force target override for declared time | Does not reset encounter, grant damage immunity or make bosses bypass scripts. |

Resolved offensive base for Burn/Poison means BasePower*Attribute*Mastery\*eligible damage modifiers BEFORE direct-hit SkillCoefficient and crit. Apply DoT-specific passive multipliers once, separately from hit modifiers. DoT snapshots travel with their source; victim mitigation/protection remains live. Periodic ticks cannot seed another copy of themselves. Final partial ticks scale by elapsed fraction for duration-based DoTs; discrete pulse skills use their own endpoint policy.

## 04.3 Control resistance and stacking defaults

NEW BASELINE control profiles: COMMON duration/displacement 1.0; ELITE hard-control duration 0.50 and displacement 0.50; BOSS no hard CC or displacement absent encounter opt-in, with eligible Freeze/Root substituting 30% Slow for 2 s; PROTECTED no hostile effect. Each successful hard-control application within a rolling 10 s window uses duration multipliers 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, then 0 for the fourth and later. Taunt is a separate override channel, not a stun. Slow effects use the strongest magnitude, capped 60% movement slowdown; they do not multiply to zero speed. Entity classes and immunities come from authored registries, not name substring tests. No effect may reduce boss attack-animation speed to approximate a missing cooldown field.

# 05\. Progression, acquisition and economy profiles

## 05.1 Character XP and biome awards

XPnext(L) \= roundHalfUpTo10\[100\*L^1.6\*(1+5\*(max(0,L-80)/18)^3)\]  
L=1..98; level99 is capped; cumulativeXP(1)=0  
RewardBase(Lenemy) \= roundHalfUp\[100\*Lenemy^1.6 / K(Lenemy)\]  
K \= piecewiseLinear(L, \[(1,10),(20,10),(40,14),(60,18),(80,24),(98,32),(99,32)\])  
EnemyXP \= roundHalfUp(RewardBase \* RankMultiplier \* RarityMultiplier \* LevelDifferenceFactor)

MD-02 deliberately removes endgame pressure from the reward numerator. A common equal-level kill therefore gives about 1/K of an ordinary level before 80, then progressively less. At 98 the sixfold requirement multiplier implies about 192 equal-level common kills, not 32\. The K anchors come from the source bands, but linear interpolation replaces abrupt band jumps: a higher-level common enemy must not become worth less XP merely because the next biome begins. These are equivalent-kill targets, not promised hours. Travel, density, encounter length, support contribution and reward multipliers determine real pacing; instrument and tune only after connected measurements.

Biome bands inherited as RPG design, not vanilla levels: Emerald Wilds 1..20, Howling Sands 21..40, Whisperfrost 41..60, Devastated Lands 61..80, authored endgame/difficulty variants 81..99. Use the explicit table in the appendix. Record actual biome IDs and spawn-context combat levels in the audited enemy registry. Never grant higher XP merely because an enemy was dragged across a biome border. Unknown roles are XP-disabled until classified; development fixtures use explicit test roles.

Rank multipliers: Common 1, Specialist 1.5, Elite 2.5, Miniboss 6, Boss 15\. Rarity multipliers: ordinary 1, rare-spawn 1.5, unique 2; bosses do not stack an additional unique multiplier. Level differences use enemy minus player: at least+5 \-\>1.15; \-2..+4 \-\>1; \-5..-3 \-\>.75; \-10..-6 \-\>.40; at most-11 \-\>.10. NEW BASELINE anti-boost eligibility requires contributing to the encounter and being within 64 m at death; no credit across unloaded worlds. Summoned/revived/conversion actors, training dummies and player-owned farmable entities grant no enemy rewards.

In a party, create one reward pot per enemy using the common encounter profile, then distribute equal shares to eligible members (minimum 1 XP if positive). No new multiplicative party bonus initially. Eligibility includes at least one genuine damage, non-overheal healing of a contributor, absorbed hostile damage, or effective CC/taunt contribution within 20 s. Support is not forced to last-hit. Use server event IDs and persistent reward-ledger deduplication; death processing order cannot double credit a summoned killer and its owner.

## 05.2 Skill learning and source validation

Each named source assignment in the catalog is PROPOSED until its actual NPC behaviour is verified or the signature is authored into its kit. All 21 UNASSIGNED skills can be granted by protected development commands but cannot appear in production acquisition rolls. Rank ceilings remain Common Tier I, Specialist II, Elite III, Miniboss IV, Boss V. A difficulty label alone does not authorize a new signature or ignore source identity.

NEW BASELINE LearnChance: Common acquisition rarity 15%, Rare 5%, Unique 2%. FinalChance=clamp(BaseChance+min(.40,.0015\*E(WIS)), 0,.95). The additive Wisdom boost is inherited and intentionally visible; it makes high-Wisdom learning substantially easier, so monitor it rather than quietly substituting a multiplicative formula. After ceil(3/BaseChance) eligible unsuccessful defeats of that exact source, guarantee the next eligible learn (20/60/150 failures respectively). This pity counter does not change with equipment swaps. Already learned skills do not reroll, award physical skill items, or grant bonus passives.

One signature opportunity per eligible player/source defeat, independent of last-hit. SourceValidationState must pass VERIFIED\_CONNECTED before public unlock rolls. Rarity reflects encounter scarcity and acquisition difficulty, not number of source enemies. Preserve source uniqueness across aliases/patrol copies; different variants require an explicit different authored combat identity. Do not invent a new source simply to eliminate UNASSIGNED rows.

## 05.3 Skill mastery

NEW BASELINE skillLevel 1..20; XPnext Mastery(m)=roundHalfUp(50\*m^1.5) for 1..19. Meaningful manual root results give 1 MasteryXP; no button-press credit. A long channel, Aura or summon root can earn at most 1 XP per 5 s active combat interval, not per tick, target, child or projectile. Positive evidence is actual hostile HP damage, actual ally healing, absorb consumption, or successful nonredundant control against an eligible encounter enemy. No mastery from self-cost damage, friendly sparring, full-health healing, reapplying an unchanged debuff or toggling Auras in town. Combat-only movement earns 1 XP when it avoids a registered hostile attack within 1 s, capped once/5 s; ordinary travel does not.

If a target is 11+ combat levels below the player, award no mastery. Combat encounter IDs prevent repeated captive-heal/damage loops; after 60 s of unchanged farm-like interaction, require a new eligible enemy encounter before more credit. Mastery increases only magnitude by 2% per level beyond 1, maximum 38%. Discovery and behavioural transformation remain separate from mastery and belong to skill acquisition/Links.

![Figure 7. New mastery requirement curve. Meaningful-use awards are controlled separately.][image7]

**Figure 7\. New mastery requirement curve. Meaningful-use awards are controlled separately.**

## 05.4 Passive acquisition, loadout changes and presentation

NEW BASELINE: Link Insight is a server-owned earned currency, not an item or a stat allocation. Eligible encounter kills award 1 Common/2 Specialist/3 Elite/8 Miniboss/15 Boss Insight to each eligible participant, maximum one award per enemy event. Existing passive-recipes/achievement paths may later award the same ownership type. Initial purchases use 20 Insight for FOUNDATION, 40 ADVANCED, 80 SPECIALIST; each passive catalog entry names its tier. First owned copy is unlocked by the player's first eligible use of its required family; additional copies cost the same. No random passive drop system is invented. Ownership allows at most one copy of a particular passive per Skill; using it on two skills requires two owned copies and consumes two of the six nodes.

Loadout/attribute respec is free initially, allowed only after 10 s out of hostile combat and with no pending cast. Apply is atomic; cooldowns, charges, saved shield deficit and reward counters do not reset. Empty/unconnected nodes may remain in the draft; only valid paths to an equipped Skill provide mechanical benefit. No class respec exists. Full build import/export contains stable content IDs and graph/layout data only, never XP/ownership/absolute attributes. Unknown IDs and ownership violations are rejected with a reason.

Normal is the first shipped profile. Nightmare/Hell are supported schema profiles, disabled until authored spawn/encounter/source data exists. Do not fabricate three complete world variants during core implementation. Initial difficulty combat multipliers may be configured as Normal 1 HP/1 damage, Nightmare 1.8 HP/1.35 damage, Hell 3 HP/1.8 damage, but they do not substitute for authored moves, progression levels or release validation. No difficulty-based resistance penalty is introduced in this version.

# 06\. Link compiler, compatibility and deterministic composition

## 06.1 Component-scoped eligibility

A passive is accepted only when its gate succeeds for at least one explicitly selected component of the final plan and no exclusion or conflicting group applies. Both UI and server use the same validation result model: ACCEPTED; WRONG\_FAMILY; MISSING\_CAPABILITY; EXCLUDED\_DELIVERY; CONFLICTING\_MODIFIER; NO\_SCALABLE\_FIELD; SOURCE\_UNAVAILABLE; NO\_OWNED\_COPY; BUDGET\_EXCEEDED; CYCLIC\_GRAPH; UNSUPPORTED\_BUILD. No silent no-op Link is permitted. Compatibility is not decided from a name such as “Frost” or from color.

eligible \= any(targetComponent satisfies requiredFamilies AND requiredCapabilities)  
       AND none(excludedTags)  
       AND noConflictGroups  
       AND changesAtLeastOneDeclaredField  
       AND affordableOwnershipAndGraphBudget

Examples: Expanded Radius targets Fireball.splash.radius, FrostNova.burst.radius and Pedanticism.aura.radius; it rejects plain FrostBolt.collision Radius and Managuard (self-only). Chain/Piercing/Fork target true Projectile contact carriers and reject QuickSlash, Chain Lightning's native direct-target jumps and WindCutter. Arc is an example of a future Projectile-gated support, not automatically enabled for melee because melee generates a secondary shockwave. Selflessness requires a beneficial ally-radius Aura, rejecting Managuard and hostile-only Chilling Aura. Combustion requires a Burn payload, not merelyFire; DeepFreeze requires Chill application.

## 06.2 Compilation order and graph order independence

1\. Validate ownership, node kinds, root destinations and cycle freedom.  
2\. Normalize authored skill aliases and construct base typed effect graph.  
3\. Resolve structural conversion group (e.g. MobileDomain or Orbit).  
4\. Recompute effective component families/capabilities; validate all bindings again.  
5\. Resolve targeting/geometry, then multiplicity and finite-duration operations.  
6\. Apply payload/status/magnitude operators and resource/cooldown operations.  
7\. Compile repeat/trigger controllers and scoped inheritance masks.  
8\. Estimate budgets, bind placeholder-or-approved presentation and hash the plan.

UI node coordinates, joint route length and wire ordering never alter combat order. A passive is applied once to its selected component, not again to each intermediate Joint. Multiplicative child factors are recorded as child coefficients; do not recompute the entire modifier chain twice after inheriting a snapshot. Effects introduced by one passive can accept compatible payload/geometry operations only through explicit child selectors, not blanket promotion of the root skill family.

## 06.3 Continuation and triggers

For compatible Projectile contact: apply the one legal hit payload, then choose continuation in the source-approved order Split \-\> Pierce \-\> Fork \-\> Chain \-\> Return. There is no active Split passive currently; the stage remains reserved. Terrain collision selects Ricochet \-\> Return \-\> terminate. Pierce consumes its contact credit and wins over Fork at that event. Fork creates its two children once and terminates that parent's forward carrier without generating extra terminal payloads intended only for final completion. Child inherited budgets are never refreshed. Chain chooses bounded unvisited targets; Return gets a separate leg ledger but cannot restart Fork/Chain/Ricochet.

One exclusive repeat-controller group per skill: Echo, Barrage, Multistrike, Retaliation, Critical Trigger and Kill Trigger. This initial restriction is deliberate safety/design, not an alleged PoE rule. Retaliation disables manual input; other repeats do not. All repeats inherit the committed offensive snapshot and compatible non-trigger modifiers, with no additional resource/cooldown charge except an explicit root Retaliation cast. Skill Delay applies once before primary release; its delay is not copied onto Echo. Death/crit/kill children cannot activate another repeat controller. On-kill status bursts carry their own No Recursive Proc policy.

Other initial conflicts: Vacuum versus Repulsion; Widening versus Focused Channel. Orbit conversion removes Projectile continuation capabilities, so any already linked Pierce/Fork/Chain/Return/Ricochet must be rejected at final-plan validation, not silently ignored. MobileDomain is finite and never grants Aura sustain passives. Lifeblood and Leeching cannot form a Health-spend/resource-leech feedback loop. Corpse consumers, conversion and controlled summon sacrifices cannot be generically Echoed or used by kill/crit replay controllers.

## 06.4 Root budgets and event evidence

Finite root defaults inherited/closed: maximum generation 3, 48 total spawned gameplay effects, 16 triggered secondaries, maximum 8 live summons/caster, 24 live projectile carriers/caster, 8 persistent fields/caster and 4 active Auras/caster. The last bound follows the four equipped skill slots. A paid Aura does not consume its entire 48-effect budget over its lifetime: each 1 s epoch gets at most 8 secondary gameplay events, with the same live-object limits and no retained unused credits. Cosmetic particles use a separate presentation budget and cannot erase gameplay to save visual cost.

Preflight rejects a deterministic ally oversized cast before payment. If unpredictable triggers exhaust runtime budget, stop only new derived work, emit a bounded rejection trace and keep the root's already accepted effect/cost. Never duplicate or refund. Trace fields: actor, root, parent, skill, passive, component, contentHash, eventType, tick, target, gateResult, before/after resource, actualDamage, terminal Reason and remaining Budget. Avoid per-particle production logs.

# 07\. Link Tree canvas and editing contract

The supplied board images are layout vocabulary, not a request for a live Figma dependency. The native game UI has a pannable fixed-zoom canvas. No wheel/pinch zoom. Initial exactly 12 nodes: Skill S1..S4 rectangles, Passive P1..P6 circles, Joint J1..J2 triangles; all empty and unlinked. All can be moved. The title box from the diagram is not a thirteenth gameplay node. Skill slots have fixed HUD identities even when moved around the canvas.

NEW BASELINE initial canvas positions in logical UI units: Skill nodes at(240, 320),(480, 320),(720, 320),(960, 320), Passive nodes at(180, 520),(360, 520),(540, 520),(720, 520),(900, 520),(1080, 520), joints at(470, 140),(740, 140). Square skill body 128 x 96, passive diameter 96, joint triangle 112 wide/96 high. These are layout defaults only and adapt to platform UI scaling; the user cannot zoom the board. A230-unit left panel hosts independently scrolling Skills/Passives tabs, searchable unlocked rows, names, template icons and eligibility feedback. Do not pan the library when dragging the canvas.

## 07.1 Gestures and state

Left click selects a node. Left-drag its body moves it after 4 UI-unit threshold; dragging never equips/removes content. Background middle-drag or Space+left-drag pans; wheel scrolls only the focused library. Library-row drag to a matching node equips; selectednode is not required for a directdrop. Hover a library row and pressA to equip it into the selected node of the same type. No matching selection means an explained no-op. A is consumed only while the UI has focus and a hovered row; it must not trigger player movement or a combat ability.

Drag from a visible output connector to a legal input connector to parent. Inputs highlight compatible/incompatible previews and the reason. Escape cancels an in-progress drag without changing state. A per-node context action removes content; a selected-wire context action removes only that edge. Replacing a skill/passive runs the complete downstream compatibility validator; invalid links are not committed. Apply submits a revision-checked whole-graph transaction; Cancel discards gameplay edits. Layout-only movement can persist independently after a drag ends and does not require a combat loadout change.

The pan gesture, pointer capture, arbitrary key hover detection and line renderer MUST be demonstrated in Phase 00 on the pinned build. W12 proves some event names exist, not a complete FigJam canvas implementation. If the native UI cannot produce the required interaction, present the concrete unsupported capability and an alternative for approval; do not mark the fixed/static fallback as finished. Headless runtime work may continue independently, but full UI acceptance does not pass.

## 07.2 Directed graph invariants

Skill nodes are terminal sinks: no outgoing parent edge. Passive nodes have at mostone outgoing edge to Skill or Joint and cannot receive other passives. Joint has exactlythree total ports: two incoming, one outgoing; its parent is Skill or anotherJoint. NoPassive-\>Passive, Skill-\>anything, self-edge, cycle, duplicate edge, parallel port reuse or multiple Skill sinks perconnected branch. Each Passive eventually resolves to zero orone Skill. Zero is an inactive parked node, not a hidden global passive. A Joint can remain disconnected but contributes no stats.

The three-port rule means J1(P1, P2)-\>J2(P3, J1)-\>S1 collects three passives. P4, P5, P6 may each connect directlytoS1, preserving full 6/0/0/0 specialization. Skill inputs are an expandable logical aggregate, not limited toone triangleedge. Joints provide routing only, no extra passive capacity or propagation duplication. Save graph edges and stableIDs; compile flattened passive-to-skill bindings from the graph, never maintain two independent mutable authorities.

## 07.3 Spline geometry, feedback and persistence

A wire is a cubic Bezier: B(t)=(1-t)^3 P0+3(1-t)^2 tP1+3(1-t)t^2 P2+t^3 P3. Endpoint anchors are node port positions transformed by canvaspan. Control handles extend along port normals byclamp(0.35\*endpoint Distance, 32, 180)UIunits. A segmented-line fallback renderer samples 16 segments and adds a direction arrow; it must visually read as a smooth connection atfixedscale. Curve crossings are not connections. Hit-testing a selectedwire uses 6 UIunits tolerance and excludes node hit areas. Presentation order is behind nodes; no deposition updates move endpoints immediately.

States: empty, selected, equipped-unlinked, linked-valid, draft-incompatible, unsupported-build, library-locked. Disabled skills in unavailable Slot 4 retain their slot and saved links, visibly labelled Unavailable on this build; they cannot cast. Tooltips showbase/effective range, cost, reservation, cooldown, chosen passives, affected components and explicit reasons for rejection. Asset replacements do not change Skill Id, loadout ownership orsaveformat. Persistnode XY/pan/tab selection per player/resolution profile; closing/reopening does not reset positions. Synchronize only final drag position orbounded 10 Hzpreviews, not unbounded mouse move packets.

## 07.4 Character screen contract

The RPG Character screen is a dedicated custom page in the initial implementation and opens on **C**. Its window composition intentionally follows the compact Diablo II character-sheet reference (C6): dark framed panel; character name at top; Level, current Experience and Next Level immediately below; attribute rows on the left; derived combat/resource rows on the right; remaining points clearly visible. This is layout/readability inspiration only. Do not copy Diablo II textures, fonts or copyrighted art into shipped assets. The project remains classless, so no class field is introduced.

The left attribute column contains Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom and Luck in that order. Each shows raw value and effective value in its tooltip. A plus control is enabled only when the server reports unspentAttributePoints \> 0\. Clicking plus submits AllocateAttribute(attribute,+1,expectedRevision); the client never sends an absolute stat. The right column renders authoritative derived values already owned by sections 03-05: Heavy Damage modifier, Light Damage modifier, Magic Damage modifier, Healing modifier, Skill Cooldown Recovery, Critical Hit Chance, Learn Chance, Magic Find, maximum Health, maximum Mana, maximum Stamina, and any audited native Defense/Resistance values available in the pinned build. If a native resistance does not exist or cannot be read, omit it rather than inventing a zero-valued RPG resistance system.

Opening C while Character is closed opens it; pressing C again or Escape closes it. If Link Tree is open, C closes/switches the Link Tree page and opens Character rather than stacking pages. The page is a view/controller over server state, never a second progression authority. Close/reconnect cannot commit unsent allocation. Individual \+1 allocations commit immediately and revision-check independently; a future respec workflow is separate.

The long-term target is a combined Inventory \+ Character presentation matching reference C8: retain the native-equipment/inventory composition on the left/center and use the otherwise negative space on the right for the Character panel. Current public protocol separates Page.Inventory and Page.Custom \[W24\], so Codex MUST NOT patch private client widgets or declare native docking complete without Phase 00 evidence. Until a supported merge path exists, the standalone C page is the production contract. Build the Character panel as a reusable component/view model so the later composite does not duplicate stat logic.

## 07.5 HUD composition contract

The default Hytale HUD reference C5 is the spatial baseline. RPG mode preserves the compass and nine-slot item hotbar, then adds/recomposes four elements. Public HudComponent includes Health, Mana and Stamina \[W20\], while HudManager/CustomUIHud expose custom HUD layers and visibility control \[W21,W22\]. Because the requested order/position is custom, the preferred implementation is to hide only the native resource components when necessary and render one RPG-owned resource strip whose values are read from authoritative native EntityStatMap state. Do not duplicate Health/Mana/Stamina storage.

**Level Up notice.** A horizontal notice is centered directly under the compass whenever pendingLevelUpPoints \> 0. Suggested template text is LEVEL UP \- C: CHARACTER \- {N} POINTS REMAINING. It persists across combat, page changes and reconnect until all points awarded by pending level-ups have been allocated. Ordinary bonus/quest points do not resurrect this notice unless they are explicitly marked as level-up points. The notice never auto-opens a menu.

**Four Skill slots.** Four fixed RPG skill cells appear immediately to the right of hotbar slot 9, visually aligned to the hotbar baseline. They display the four logical equipped SkillIds, template/final icon, cooldown sweep, disabled/unavailable state, reservation/upkeep warning where relevant, and the audited input glyph for each slot. The cells are not item slots and never participate in inventory drag/drop. If Slot 4 lacks a proven input binding in the pinned build, it remains visible with Unavailable on this build feedback rather than stealing another control. Reference C7 is spacing/readability inspiration only.

**Mana | Health | Stamina.** The centered resource strip above the hotbar reads left-to-right **Mana | Health | Stamina**. Each bar uses current/max values from native stats and a text/tooltip value on focus. Reservation reduces spendable Mana maximum exactly as section 03 defines; the HUD must distinguish reserved capacity from damage/missing Mana, e.g. a muted reserved segment behind the current fill. Do not infer Mana from skills or maintain a second pool.

**Experience bar.** A horizontal experience bar is divided visually into exactly ten pips. Let LevelStartXP(L)=sum\_{i=1}^{L-1} XP\_to\_Next(i) and LevelProgress=clamp((totalCharacterXP-LevelStartXP(L))/XP\_to\_Next(L),0,1) for L\<99; LevelProgress=1 at level 99\. Pip j for j=0..9 has fill clamp(10\*LevelProgress-j,0,1). Separators remain visible over the continuous fill so players can accurately say they are two bars from leveling. The XP bar is presentation only; it cannot award XP or change thresholds.

HUD layout MUST be resolution/UI-scale aware. Define anchors relative to the existing hotbar/compass rather than absolute screen pixels. Custom layers must not cover chat, reticle or native interaction prompts. On HUD teardown, world change or mod disable, restore any native components hidden by the RPG HUD.

## 07.6 Keyboard ownership and input precedence

RPG keyboard contract: **K \= Link Tree**, **C \= Character**. C is currently user-observed as the machinima/front-facing camera-flip control; RPG integration must remove C from that action so one physical press never triggers both camera reversal and Character. The reverse-camera action may remain unbound unless a later user-facing remap is approved. Tab remains Inventory. Escape closes the currently focused RPG page.

Phase 00 must identify the actual pinned-build client/input binding mechanism before implementation. CustomUIEventBindingType proves page-level key events but not arbitrary global world-state hotkeys \[W12\]. If a supported keybinding asset/config/API exists, use it and record the exact file/API plus restoration path. If no supported global remap exists, mark the C/K hotkey sub-capability BLOCKED and present evidence; do not emulate it by polling chat text, stealing movement controls, or installing an opaque native-client binary patch. The Character/Link Tree pages and HUD can continue behind protected development commands while the hotkey adapter is unresolved, but release acceptance requires the specified keys.

Input precedence: text/chat entry and focused text fields consume typing first; modal confirmations consume C/K if required by the UI framework; otherwise C/K toggle their RPG pages only from ordinary gameplay or another RPG page. Repeated key-down events are edge-triggered once per press. Server requests remain permission-checked and idempotent.

## 07.7 Future Inventory merge boundary

The standalone Character page is deliberately engineered for later docking. CharacterSheetViewModel and its component layout are reusable. When a supported Inventory composition/extension path is proven, the target page places Hytale equipment/character preview on the left, inventory/crafting content in the center, and the Character panel in right-side negative space, preserving the existing inventory interaction semantics from reference C8. Do not fork inventory containers, duplicate drag/drop code or replace server-owned ItemContainers merely to achieve the layout. Until that migration is explicitly authorized, Tab continues to open Hytale Inventory and C opens the standalone Character page.

# 08\. Art, icon, VFX and audio system: no artist dependency

## 08.1 Separate readiness states

Mechanics: PLANNED \-\> IMPLEMENTED \-\> TESTED \-\> ENABLED. Presentation: TEMPLATE \-\> CANDIDATE\_BOUND \-\> REVIEWED \-\> ART\_APPROVED. Acquisition: UNASSIGNED/PROPOSED \-\> VERIFIED\_ASSET \-\> VERIFIED\_CONNECTED. These axes are independent. An enabled skill can use TEMPLATE visuals and icons if mechanically readable. A polished VFX does not make an unassigned or untested source learnable. Previous conversational YES/NO art judgments are not API feasibility certificates.

All 87 skills and 66 passives require an iconKey. Resolution order is artist override, shipped family template, then shipped generic template. The final fallback MUST exist. Use 128x128 RGBA masters with 4px padding, a family silhouette, a two-character skill abbreviation and a reserved number band. Render HUD icons at 48px and library icons at 48/64px through the same logical key. Borders, rarity, selection, cooldown and reservation overlays are runtime UI layers, not baked into the artist's PNG. Use a dark opaque backplate so readability does not depend on the scene behind it. Stable content IDs allow artwork replacement without changing code or saves.

Template geometry: Projectile uses an arrow; Strike a slash; Aura a ring; GroundZone concentric discs; Beam parallel streaks; Movement a chevron; Summon geometric paw-like dots; Barrier a shield pentagon; DirectTarget a crosshair; Trap a diamond; CorpseOperation a broken ring; Stance double brackets; Reaction a return arrow. These are generated shapes, not required bespoke illustrations. They are explicitly temporary art. Artist replacements are optional asset-pack overrides validated for dimensions, alpha and the stable key. No mechanics phase requires the final icon library.

## 08.2 Real particle evidence and safe fallback

W01 is an author-maintained historical catalog with 535 names, edited January 20, 2026\. It includes cold, beam, shield, aura and void candidates beyond the five particles in the older technical document. Candidate names are listed per skill, but catalog membership does not prove availability, visual quality, attachment compatibility or endpoint fitting in the installed build. W02/W03 describe particle asset schemas; W04/W05 describe projectile/effect references and attachment-related fields. HTDevLib is optional; project-owned lifecycle and cleanup must not depend on the helper's internals \[W16\].

In Phase 00, export the installed particle systems, spawners, textures, models, trails, sounds and animations. Each audit record contains asset ID, path, hash, type, source pack, loop/lifespan, attachment requirements and build hash. Record a short in-game preview for every candidate actually adopted. IDs are case-sensitive. Beam\_Lightning2 and IceBall are documented candidates, not invented RPG asset names. Names containing Example or Old are not automatically final-quality assets.

Recipe resolution order is: reviewed current-build native/custom asset; inspected current-build candidate; shipped RPG procedural template. A missing candidate emits one bounded diagnostic and selects its fallback without disabling mechanics. A malformed fallback, absent required telegraph or unsafe infinite emitter fails content preflight. Each layer owns a start offset, anchor, rotation, scale, opacity, tint mode, duration, emission cadence, LOD and termination handle. Tint is supported only after visual testing; asset-specific colors can override packet-level color settings.

RPG\_Template\_Bolt, RPG\_Template\_Burst, RPG\_Template\_Ring, RPG\_Template\_Beam, RPG\_Template\_Glyph, RPG\_Template\_Shield, RPG\_Template\_Shards and RPG\_Template\_Summon are NEW project asset names to create, not claimed vanilla IDs. Generate their PNG sprites and simple model geometry, then encode the particle/model assets against the pinned schema. A bolt must have a visible core; a beam must show its endpoint; a zone must show its footprint; a cage must have visible boundaries. Distinctive aura, scythe, root and void artwork can replace these later without rewriting mechanics.

## 08.3 Visual language and deterministic geometry

Initial art palette: Physical warm steel/amber; Fire orange/white; Cold pale cyan/white; Magic blue/violet; Lightning white/electric blue; Earth ochre/stone gray; Wind off-white/teal; Void violet/teal with a dark core; Necrotic ivory/muted violet; Poison yellow-green; Nature leaf green; Holy gold/white. Color is not the only state cue. Use family shape, distinctive motion and different friendly/hostile boundary patterns. Ground warnings must not obscure the actors or their weapons.

Camera shake defaults off. Optional heavy-impact feedback is capped at 0.15 degrees for 0.15 seconds and affects only the local recipient; do not change aim or server position. Avoid full-screen flashes. Existing creature animations can remain on summoned creature models; they do not need to be retargeted onto the player's humanoid rig. Scythe Sweep uses a humanoid action with a weapon-shaped visual, not new creature anatomy.

OrbitPosition(t) \= centre \+ (r\*cos(theta), height, r\*sin(theta))  
theta \= initialPhase \+ angularSpeed\*t  
WarningProgress(t) \= clamp((t-warningStart)/warningDuration, 0, 1\)  
BurstVisualRadius(t) \= authoredRadius\*clamp(t/0.30, 0, 1\)  
BeamSegmentCount \= clamp(ceil(length/0.5), 2, 64\)

Projectile trails follow replicated authoritative motion, including steering. Warning progress and visual ring expansion cannot schedule extra damage. Templates sit 0.10m above the ground to avoid z-fighting without changing hit geometry. Beam endpoints come from the actual LOS query. Cone visuals use authored range and half-angle. Bone Cage collision is independent of its visible posts; showing a rock or wall model never grants terrain modification.

## 08.4 Audio and presentation budgets

No reliable exact sound-event catalog was obtained for this master. Use semantic keys for native weapon release/hit, elemental spell release/impact, Aura start/stop, summon spawn/despawn, shield break and control application. Phase 00 resolves them to verified sound IDs. Reuse native equipped-weapon events first. A missing optional audio accent falls back to silence with a diagnostic, not an invented sound ID or a mechanics failure. Initial pitch range is 0.9..1.1 and gain 0..1 per inspected asset. Aggregate repeated impacts to at most one voice per target per 0.10s.

Initial per-client presentation budget is 128 active particle-system handles and 32 simultaneous audio voices. Important warnings take priority over ambient layers. Cull ambient effects after 40m and impact accents after 64m; required ability warnings must remain visible across the actual relevant combat range. Under pressure, remove ambient motes before telegraphs. Cosmetic limits cannot change hit results. Every recipe has one owner and explicit stop/removal handles; prefer finite-emission loops over unowned eternal systems.

**Look and feel:** An overhead crown-like diamond and allied outline replace the hostile marker for twelve seconds; expiration has a brief warning blink before allegiance restores.

**Timing and ownership:** Footprint preview follows exact server geometry; use declared warning/duration/ticks. Instant burst expansion 0.30 s is presentation-only. Persistent ambient layer stops immediately on cancellation, with non-gameplay fade\<=0.30 s.

**Candidate SystemIds \[W01\]:** Effect\_Crown\_Gold, Magic\_Hit.

**Fallback / art acceptance:** procedural direct\_target template; element palette VOID; exact gameplay footprint/telegraph preserved. Template is acceptable for functional gates when range, allies/enemies, source ownership and effect lifetime are readable; artist approval is a separate ART\_APPROVED state.

**Icon / VFX keys:** rpg.icon.skill.dominate / rpg.vfx.skill.dominate. Audio uses the family/element semantic keys from08.4; no unverified SoundId is mandatory.

# 10\. Complete passive catalog: 66 gated contracts

Source: S2 section6. The Exact Baseline Effect is preserved, including the accepted Echo and Skill Delay. Fleeting from an earlier chat proposal is not in the frozen66-entry source and is not reintroduced. Master supplements close missing constants, component ownership and exclusions; they do not authorize double application of an inherited modifier. New exclusions are conservative initial gates and are revisable only by a versioned design change. Passives use stable placeholder icons through the same resolver as active skills.

## LP-001. Potency

rpg.passive.potency • Phase 06 • FOUNDATION • 20 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Payload: Damage, Heal, or Barrier; scalable magnitude.

**Exact baseline effect:** Increase the linked skill's damage, healing, or barrier magnitude by 15%.

**Execution / interactions:** Uses the normal Increased modifier bucket. Does not change status duration, radius, resource cost, or control strength unless those values are derived directly from the affected payload.

**Master parameters / safety:** Magnitude whitelist: direct damage, DoT DPS, healing and absorb capacity only; no cooldown, reservation, CC or Emanatism/Pedanticism utility coefficients.

**Fixture:** accept Quick Slash; reject Emanatism (No scalable damage/healing/barrier payload). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-002. Efficiency

rpg.passive.efficiency • Phase 11 • FOUNDATION • 20 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Finite Mana/Stamina cost or continuous Mana upkeep; excludes pure Mana Reservation.

**Exact baseline effect:** Reduce the linked skill's declared spend cost or continuous upkeep by 15%.

**Execution / interactions:** Never reduces Mana Reservation percentages. Cost floors at 1 for non-zero integer costs. Reservation Auras use Conservation instead.

**Master parameters / safety:** Integer upfront cost \= max(1, ceil(baseCost\*factor)); upkeep retains fractional precision with 0.25 s quanta. Zero remains zero.

**Fixture:** accept Fireball; reject Managuard (Reservation is not an upfront spend). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-003. Long Reach

rpg.passive.long\_reach • Phase 11 • FOUNDATION • 20 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: HasRange.

**Exact baseline effect:** Increase target range, projectile maximum travel distance, beam/line/tether reach, or movement destination range by 25%.

**Execution / interactions:** Does not increase radius, cone angle, line width, Aura radius, or projectile collision size. A skill must expose a range parameter to qualify.

**Master parameters / safety:** Each declared range field gets 1.25 once. Placement distance is distinct from radius and collision extents; no multiplying nested same field twice.

**Fixture:** accept Frost Bolt; reject Managuard (No range field). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-004. Rapid Invocation

rpg.passive.rapid\_invocation • Phase 11 • FOUNDATION • 20 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: HasCastTime; excludes Instant-only, Toggle-only, and Reaction-only skills.

**Exact baseline effect:** Reduce pre-execution cast/activation time by 20%.

**Execution / interactions:** Does not accelerate channel tick rate, projectile travel, delayed payload timing, cooldown, or animation playback after the cast commits.

**Master parameters / safety:** Wind-up multiplier 0.80; minimum 0.05 s for nonzero wind-up. Cannot accelerate Skill Delay or telegraph warning below its declared duration.

**Fixture:** accept Heavy Swing; reject Quick Slash (No nonzero cast time). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-005. Second Wind

rpg.passive.second\_wind • Phase 11 • SPECIALIST • 80 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: HasCooldown \+ DiscreteActivation; excludes Aura, Channel, Stance, Transformation, and indefinite Toggle skills.

**Exact baseline effect:** Grant the linked skill one additional stored charge, but increase recharge/cooldown time by 30%.

**Execution / interactions:** Each charge pays the normal resource cost. Charge recharge is server-authoritative. The passive is invalid for skills whose state is maintained continuously rather than activated discretely.

**Master parameters / safety:** Base charges 1-\>2; one serial recharge queue; recharge begins when a charge is spent. Persist charge recovery time; swapping/relogging never refills charges.

**Fixture:** accept Quickstep; reject Emanatism (Indefinite toggle cannot store charges). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

**Execution / interactions:** Cost is modified before affordability validation. Pure reservation skills do not qualify because their resource commitment is governed by Aura-specific passives.

**Fixture:** accept Fireball; reject Pedanticism (Pure reservation/utility effect). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

## LP-007. Concentration

rpg.passive.concentration • Phase 11 • SPECIALIST • 80 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: HasAreaGeometry \+ scalable payload.

**Exact baseline effect:** Increase linked damage/healing/barrier effect by 30%, but reduce its affected geometry scale by 30%.

**Execution / interactions:** Applies to Burst, Ground Zone, Area of Effect, Aura, Vortex/Pull, Cone, Line, Wall, and other explicitly area-capable families. Geometry reduction uses the family's authored radius/width/length rule rather than blindly scaling every number.

**Fixture:** accept Ground Slam; reject Snipe (No area payload). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

## LP-008. Expanded Radius

rpg.passive.expanded\_radius • Phase 06 • FOUNDATION • 20 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: HasRadius.

## LP-009. Lingering

## LP-010. Echo

rpg.passive.echo • Phase 06 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Capability: SpellCast \+ DiscreteActivation; excludes Strike/weapon attacks, Aura, Channel, Stance, Reaction, Triggered, Transformation, Movement, Summon, and Deployable.

**Exact baseline effect:** After the primary execution, automatically execute the linked spell a second time after 0.45 seconds at 70% effect. The echo pays no additional resource cost and does not start another cooldown.

**Execution / interactions:** The echo reuses the committed target solution when still valid and inherits the compiled non-trigger modifiers. It cannot Echo itself. If Skill Delay is also linked, the primary execution is delayed first; Echo schedules 0.45 seconds after that primary execution and does not re-apply Skill Delay.

**Master parameters / safety:** One repeat group per skill: conflicts with Barrage, Multistrike, Retaliation, Critical Trigger, Kill Trigger. Exclude corpse/summon consumers and collision-wall creators. Repeat uses original world target; revalidate target/range/LOS and cancel if invalid.

**Fixture:** accept Frost Bolt; reject Quick Slash (Weapon Strike is not eligible discrete SpellCast). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-011. Piercing

rpg.passive.piercing • Phase 07 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Family: Projectile; capability: CanPierce.

**Exact baseline effect:** Allow each projectile to pierce 2 additional enemy contacts.

**Execution / interactions:** Pierce consumes the enemy-contact continuation budget before Fork or Chain. A target may be damaged only once per outbound phase unless another modifier explicitly creates a new phase.

**Master parameters / safety:** Contacts consume 2 continuation credits; same entity ignored for 0.10 s and recorded for outbound leg. Root event order preserves hit payload before continuation.

**Fixture:** accept Snipe; reject Wind Cutter (Line is not Projectile). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

## LP-012. Fork

rpg.passive.fork • Phase 07 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Family: Projectile; capability: CanFork.

**Exact baseline effect:** When forward Pierce is exhausted, fork the projectile into 2 child projectiles at the next valid enemy contact.

**Execution / interactions:** Child projectiles inherit legal projectile modifiers, consume root-cast spawn budgets, and cannot Fork again unless a future passive explicitly raises fork generation. Continuation order remains Split \-\> Pierce \-\> Fork \-\> Chain \-\> Return.

**Master parameters / safety:** Branches at-20/+20 degrees around incoming horizontal direction; effect factor 1.0 each, same remaining distance budget, each child records the hit target as already visited. Fork depth 1\.

**Fixture:** accept Fire Bolt; reject Quick Slash (Wrong delivery family). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-013. Chain

rpg.passive.chain • Phase 07 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Family: Projectile; capability: CanChain.

**Exact baseline effect:** After its current enemy-contact continuation resolves, redirect the projectile/effect to up to 2 additional nearby enemies.

**Execution / interactions:** Each chained target must be unique within that chain sequence. Chain selection is server-authoritative and range-bounded. Chain occurs after Fork and before Return.

**Master parameters / safety:** Nearest unvisited enemy within 8 mLOS, deterministic distance then stable-ID tie break; no distance budget reset. Native DirectTarget Chain Lightning cannot accept this Projectile-only passive.

**Fixture:** accept Fire Bolt; reject Chain Lightning (DirectTarget native chain is not Projectile). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

**Presentation:** Reuse the linked skill's icon with an external passive badge; update affected telegraph geometry/timing, not just the tooltip. Repeats and child effects inherit the family template and owner cleanup. No bespoke passive art is a mechanics requirement.

## LP-014. Ricochet

rpg.passive.ricochet • Phase 07 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Family: Projectile; capability: CanTerrainBounce.

**Exact baseline effect:** Allow up to 2 terrain ricochets before the projectile terminates.

**Execution / interactions:** Uses server collision normals and a dedicated terrain-bounce budget. Ricochet does not count as enemy Chain. Return begins only after the forward terrain/enemy continuation path is exhausted.

**Master parameters / safety:** vNew \= v-2\*dot(v, n)\*n; speed preserved, offset 0.03 m from surface, maximum 2; minimum bounce interval 0.05 s. Never phase through terrain.

**Fixture:** accept Fire Bolt; reject Frost Nova (No terrain-bouncing projectile). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.

## LP-015. Return

rpg.passive.return • Phase 07 • ADVANCED • 40 Insight/copy

**Compatibility gate:** Family: Projectile; capability: CanReturn.

**Exact baseline effect:** After the projectile exhausts its normal forward path, send it back toward the caster.

**Execution / interactions:** Outbound and return phases maintain separate hit ledgers so a target may be hit once on the outbound path and once on the return path. Return does not restart Fork/Chain/Ricochet budgets.

**Master parameters / safety:** Return speed equals compiled outgoing speed; return travel budget \= compiled max distance, safety lifetime distance/speed+0.1 s. Chase live caster but terminate at first solid obstacle or within 0.5 m of caster.

**Fixture:** accept Snipe; reject Void Beam (Beam has no return leg). Maximum one copy per skill. Display the rejected gate in UI and revalidate it server-side.
